title: Orchestrator lock lease expiry caused stalled rollout and mitigations
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: During a routine canary promotion on 2025-02-24 the orchestrator observed a lease expiry on the promotion lock for a subset of route masters. That expiry produced an inconsistent view across region replicas which caused traffic to (a) keep routing to the old variant in some AZs and (b) fail automatic rollback in others due to a dual-locked state. Result: a 17-minute period where 6% of requests received mixed-variant responses and automatic rollback remained blocked by a 'lease-starvation' condition. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations applied, and proposed long-term actions to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2025-02-24T09:14:11Z - Orchestrator master in us-west-2 observed lease renewal failure (network blip to metadata service)
2025-02-24T09:14:45Z - Lease expired on leader for shard S-12; new leader elected but some region replicas had stale route metadata
2025-02-24T09:16:00Z - Traffic began to split inconsistently: us-west-1 continued serving old variant, eu-west-1 served canary; tokenized requests hit mixed KV cache states
2025-02-24T09:21:05Z - Automatic rollback attempted but was blocked by a second lock acquisition failure (lease contention) leading to rollback deadlock
2025-02-24T09:31:30Z - Mitigation: ops forced a coordinated orchestration fencing sequence and rolled back canary manually; traffic reunited on stable variant
2025-02-24T09:40:00Z - All routes stabilized; incident declared resolved at 09:42 after monitoring showed consistent variant assignment for 10 minutes
root_cause: A combination of short-lived metadata service connectivity hiccup and an orchestrator lock implementation that assumes fast lease renewal. The lock lease timeout and renewal window were too tight for sustained small network jitter, causing the original leader to appear dead and a partially completed leader-election to leave some replicas with stale route metadata. Additionally, KV cache tombstones (old seq IDs) were not reconciled during the mid-election state which allowed mixed-serve for certain request prefixes. The rollback logic required acquiring the same lock and failed when quorum was temporary inconsistent, producing a deadlock instead of a safe unwind path.
immediate_actions_taken: 1) Ops executed a coordinated fencing and forced-rollover sequence to ensure a single authoritative leader for each shard. 2) Reconciled route metadata across replicas using the route-fanout reconciler (one-time run). 3) Manually triggered full KV prefix sync for affected shards. 4) Increased alerting thresholds and added a short-lived runbook so on-call could identify lease expiry patterns faster. 5) Disabled automatic rollback for the specific rollout path until fixes land.
long_term_action_items: Increase lock lease renewal window and make renewal adaptive to observed metadata service latency (owner: infra/orchestrator, estimate: 3)
Add a conservative leader-fencing mechanism: require quorum-ack of metadata reconciliation before allowing promotion in multi-region rollouts (owner: orchestrator, estimate: 5)
Make rollback code path idempotent and tolerant to transient lock acquisition failures by implementing a safe-unwind state machine (owner: runtime-serving, estimate: 8)
Add KV cache reconciliation step during leader-election that zeroes tombstones for prefixes active in the last X minutes (owner: kv-cache, estimate: 5)
Instrument new metrics: lease_expiry_rate, leader-election-duration, stale-route-count, rollback-fence-failures and wire into console alerts with runbook links (owner: observability, estimate: 3)
Run a chaos test in staging that simulates short metadata service outages for rolling promotions and validate no mixed-serve or blocked rollbacks (owner: reliability, due: 2025-03-25, estimate: 2)
Post-incident documentation/update: add 'orchestrator lease expiry' play to runbook and schedule training for SRE/on-call (owner: ops, due: 2025-03-15)
Review and harden default rollout timeout and backoff parameters in the console UI with clearer guardrails for customers (owner: console, estimate: 3)
reviewers_feedback: PM (Ravi Patel): prioritize idempotent rollback and safe-unwind state machine — high customer impact if rollbacks block
Design (Elena Park): console should surface 'promotion pending reconciliation' state to avoid accidental re-promotes from UI
Security (Jonah Reed): no direct security impact but ensure reconciliation does not expose stale auth metadata
SRE (Lila Morgan): recommend conservative defaults for lease windows and add synthetic checks in control-plane health dashboard
next_steps: 1) Triage PRs above and schedule merge window for lease-renewal tuning and safe-unwind prototype in next release train. 2) Run staging chaos test by 2025-03-20. 3) Ship observability metrics and console UI guardrails by 2025-04-01. 4) Close this ticket when all long-term action items are either merged and deployed to canary or have an accepted exceptions/mitigation.
